A-perf-02.argument: In system/mod.rs the seven entity index HashMaps (:69-81) plus stage_index (:94) carry serde(skip) and are rebuilt by rebuild_indices (:588) from From<SystemRepr> (:221); the in-file rationale (:64-68) is that serializing an unstable-iteration-order map makes the wire payload non-reproducible for identical content. cascade (:85) and network (:87) carry NO skip, appear in SystemRepr (:157-158), and the From body takes repr.cascade/repr.network verbatim (:198-199), so their five HashMaps (downstream, upstream, bus_lines, bus_generators, bus_loads) ride the postcard payload that broadcast_value(raw_system, ...) serializes and broadcasts to every rank (cobre-cli setup.rs:322 -> broadcast.rs postcard::to_allocvec). Both are content-determined derivations of entity bytes serialized ahead of them, so every rank can rebuild them locally exactly as the indices are; serializing their HashMaps also reintroduces the same order-instability the index-skip was written to avoid.

The defensible residue is that cascade+network's five HashMaps are transmitted on the wire despite being pure, content-determined derivations of the seven entity slices already serialized ahead of them in the same struct, and thus locally reconstructible in rebuild_indices.
A-perf-02.title: The MPI broadcast payload carries the two derived topologies (`cascade`, `network`) that every rank could rebuild locally, while the sibling index maps three fields above are skipped and rebuilt

B-perf-00.argument: At baseline `tokenize` (generic.rs:629) is reached only via `parse_relation` <- `convert`'s per-constraint load-time loop (line 489) — the constraint-file-to-struct conversion, never the SDDP training/simulation hot paths enumerated in architecture-rules.md. The `Vec<char>` collect (line 631) is deliberate: it gives O(1) indexed two-char lookahead (`chars.get(i+1)` for `==`/`<=`/`>=`) and lets every error report a char-offset position (`at position {i}`) a human counting characters can locate; the grammar accepts Unicode identifier starts (`is_alphabetic`), so a byte-offset rewrite would silently shift those reported positions on the non-ASCII rejection path. Owned `Token::Ident`/`ParamRef` strings (lines 623/625) keep tokens `'static` and independent of the input's lifetime. The per-token allocations (709/720/735) are linear in a bounded authored expression and paid once at study load, so they are not a hot-path allocation violation and the design reason justifies the current code.
B-perf-00.title: The generic-constraint tokenizer copies each expression into a `Vec<char>` and allocates a fresh `String` for every identifier and numeric literal instead of borrowing the input

B-perf-01.argument: The evidence resolves at baseline: `inline` (named_expression_inline.rs:57) builds its `HashMap<&str,&ParsedExpression>` index per top-level call, and `resolve_split_side` (generic.rs:1254-1255) does a linear `table.iter().any(...)` membership scan then calls `inline(&vec![...],table)`, rebuilding the index and allocating a one-element Vec for a single reference. Both call sites run inside `convert`'s per-constraint load-time loop (line 489), not a hot path. `table` is the named-expression declaration table, documented-bounded to 'tens of expressions x tens of terms' (MAX_INLINED_TERMS doc), so a tens-entry HashMap built per constraint is trivial; and within one `inline` call the index is built once and shared across the full transitive `inline_into` recursion (passed by `&`), so it is not per-term inside a constraint's expansion. `inline`'s slice-taking signature is a self-contained entry-point contract, and the relational double-lookup applies only to bound-position `@`-refs. These load-time costs over a bounded table justify the current design.
B-perf-01.title: Named-expression inlining rebuilds the whole name index on every call, and the relational path pays a linear table scan plus a throwaway one-element vector per reference term

B-perf-02.argument: Confirmed at baseline: `resolve_coverage_gated_observations` (estimation.rs:468-479) nests, per hydro, an `occurrences` loop over a `.filter(...).map(...).collect()` across all of that hydro's `windows`, so the comparison count is O(occurrences x windows) and both grow with historical record depth — quadratic in an unbounded dimension. The monotonicity the linear alternative needs is genuinely present: `parse_inflow_history` sorts rows by (hydro_id,start_date) (inflow_history.rs:137) and `validate_windowed_records` rejects per-entity overlap (windowed_history.rs), so each per-hydro `windows` slice is ascending and disjoint; `discover_hydro_occurrences` yields `BTreeMap::into_values()`, ascending. A monotone-join sweep would be O(N+M) and the per-occurrence throwaway `Vec<RealizedWindow>` copy is a contiguous subslice. This runs at study setup (single entry stochastic_pipeline.rs), but 'runs once' does not excuse quadratic scaling in an unbounded dimension. Narrowed: the second anchor `check_std_ratio_divergence` (line 842) scans (hydros x seasons), bounded, which does NOT scale with record depth.
B-perf-02.survivingClaim: The projection join at estimation.rs:468-479 is O(occurrences x windows) per hydro — quadratic in unbounded historical record depth — plus a per-occurrence throwaway `Vec<RealizedWindow>` copy of what is a contiguous subslice of the already-sorted, provably-disjoint `windows`; the second anchor (check_std_ratio_divergence:842) is a bounded (hydros x seasons) scan that does not scale with record depth and is not part of the surviving defect.
B-perf-02.title: The stochastic estimator resolves per-group work by re-scanning a whole table once per group, making history-window projection quadratic in record depth

B-perf-03.argument: Mechanism confirmed at baseline: `parse_inflow_history` (inflow_history.rs:144-152) maps every parsed `InflowHistoryRow` into a parallel `Vec<WindowedRecord>` consumed only by `validate_windowed_records` on the next line, then dropped. Avoiding it needs a generic accessor/iterator boundary — added complexity for a load-time linear copy. The abstraction cost is justified.
B-perf-03.title: Inflow-history parsing materializes a second full copy of the table solely to call the shared windowed-record validator

So the comment at scenarios.rs:459 ('Config is Layer-2-validated, so these reads do not fail in practice') is not underwritten: the five admission rules in `validate_scenario_source_cfg`/`validate_openings_cfg` fire only inside the accessor (reached via `convert_scenario_source_config` at :227-228), and cobre-io's nine call sites (scenarios.rs 274/284/462/468/550, season.rs 255, stages.rs 299/643/773) all discard the error via let-else or `.ok()`. cobre-io's own load path therefore never rejects an invalid scenario-source config. It is not an end-to-end silent-accept though: `cobre validate` (validate.rs:382), SDDP setup (setup/mod.rs:385), and cobre-python all re-call the accessor with `?`/`map_err`, so every current production entry point closes the gap out-of-pipeline.
C-architecture-00.survivingClaim: The scenario-source admission rules are enforced only lazily inside the accessor and cobre-io's own load pipeline (`run_pipeline`) never rejects an invalid config, the nine let-else/`.ok()` swallows resting on a false premise comment at scenarios.rs:459 that `validate_config` does not establish; but rejection is not lost end-to-end because each consumer (validate.rs:382, setup/mod.rs:385, cobre-python) re-propagates, so the defect is a mislocated/duplicated admission gate, not a production silent-accept.
C-architecture-00.title: The config admission rules are enforced only as a side effect of an accessor, and every cobre-io caller discards the resulting error on a premise the Layer-2 gate does not satisfy

C-architecture-01.argument: The predicate pairs coincide at the baseline: cobre-core `validate_line_refs` (validate.rs:131) and cobre-io `check_line_references` (referential.rs:95) both test `source_bus_id`/`target_bus_id` against the bus registry, and the filling guard `entry_stage_id.is_none()` under a present `filling` appears in both crates (validate.rs:301, hydro.rs:335). The only production `SystemBuilder::build` is pipeline.rs:248, which runs after `ctx.into_result()?` at :99 (every other `.build()` is in `#[cfg(test)]`), so in production cobre-io aborts first and the cobre-core copy of each overlapping rule never fires, letting the two drift undetected. `LoadError::CrossReferenceError` (error.rs:65) has zero production producers workspace-wide (error.rs:204 and cli/error.rs:460 are tests; python io.rs/errors.rs only consume) because the referential layer routes findings through `ValidationContext` into `ConstraintError`. cobre-core's builder validation is legitimate defense-in-depth for its public builder used by direct/test constructors, so a wholesale delete-one-side over-reaches; and moving hydro/stage rules down into cobre-core would trip the layering guardrail, which the narrowed residue does not require.
C-architecture-01.survivingClaim: Confirmed narrowly: `LoadError::CrossReferenceError` is a dead variant (zero production producers, findings routed through `ConstraintError`) retaining two cobre-python consumer arms, and the overlapping line/hydro-filling predicate pairs can drift undetected because only cobre-io's copy fires in the production pipeline, not that cobre-core's builder validation is itself redundant (it legitimately guards cobre-core's public builder for direct/test constructors).
C-architecture-01.title: Entity referential and filling invariants are implemented twice — cobre-io Layer 3/5a and cobre-core `SystemBuilder::build` — with the cobre-core copy unreachable through the only production build path

C-architecture-02.argument: Two rules of the bound-override family are implemented twice at the baseline. Block-id-range: block_bounds.rs `check_row` emits `ErrorKind::BusinessRuleViolation` (:200) for six families, while referential.rs `check_generic_constraint_bounds_validity` emits `ErrorKind::InvalidValue` (:804) for the seventh, the same user defect classified two ways. Duplicate-row: block_bounds.rs keys per column `(entity_id, group_id, stage_id, block_id, column)` (DuplicateRowKey at :351) and its doc treats disjoint-column rows for one (entity,stage,block) as legitimate sparse input, whereas referential.rs keys per row `(constraint_id, stage_id, block_id)` (:885), so the identical deck shape is rejected for generic constraint bounds and accepted for the other six. `check_ncs_bounds_and_factors` (:955) also places a pure value check (`available_generation_mw < 0.0` as `InvalidValue`) in Layer 3, whose header (:1-8) scopes the module to cross-entity references only. All confirmed by reading the two modules.
C-architecture-02.survivingClaim: Confirmed as-scoped to two concrete divergences: the block-id-range defect is `BusinessRuleViolation` in block_bounds.rs but `InvalidValue` in referential.rs, and the duplicate-row rule keys per-column in Layer 5a versus per-row in Layer 3 so a disjoint-column duplicate is legal for six families and rejected for generic constraint bounds; plus the NCS negative-value check sits in the reference-only Layer 3 module.
C-architecture-02.title: The bound-override rule family is split across two validation layers by entity family, and the two halves disagree on both `ErrorKind` and duplicate-key granularity for the same defect

C-architecture-03.argument: The dangling-reference idiom (message '<Row>[i] references non-existent <Entity> <id> via field <field>', `ErrorKind::InvalidReference`) is written out 48 times across 13 functions in referential.rs, and the module header at :22-24 prints the shared template as a literal comment rather than one definition; check_scenario_references (:366) shows the hand-copied block. The same station already table-drives the analogous shape via `FamilyMeta` (block_bounds.rs:25) plus shared emit helpers, and the study-stage predicate `filter(|s| s.id >= 0)` is restated 20 times across 11 modules while `StageIdResolver` (stage_resolve.rs:31/53) owns `study_stage_ids`. But not all 48 blocks are mechanically collapsible: hydro references carry Option-valued (`downstream_id`, `diversion.downstream_id`) and per-plant-scoped (`hydro_group_bus`) logic a flat descriptor table would not capture, so a claim that one table replaces all 48 over-reaches. The confirmable residue is the redundant restatement of the uniform flat-membership blocks and of the study-stage predicate despite in-crate precedents.
C-architecture-03.survivingClaim: Confirmed narrowly: the uniform flat 'field is in id-set' reference blocks and the 20 copies of the `s.id >= 0` study-stage predicate are open-coded despite in-crate precedents (`FamilyMeta` table, `StageIdResolver`), and the header comment stands in for one message-template definition, conceding that Option-valued, nested, and per-plant-scoped references are not mechanically table-collapsible, so the residue is redundant idiom restatement rather than a single table replacing all 48 blocks.
C-architecture-03.title: The foreign-key and study-stage idioms are open-coded across the validation layer while a table-driven precedent for the same shape already exists in the same station

C-architecture-04.argument: The numbered semantic-rule registry is a prose table in semantic/mod.rs with no code binding: rules dispatch through two hand-maintained lists (validate_semantic_hydro_thermal and validate_semantic_stages_penalties_scenarios at :188) with nothing tying a table row to its implementing function. Row 26 (:105) claims a live rule for `simulation.sampling_scheme.type` with `ErrorKind::InvalidValue`, but that field no longer exists on `SimulationConfig`; `deny_unknown_fields` rejects it at parse as the config test at config/mod.rs:1429-1447 pins (ParseError/SchemaError, not InvalidValue), and grepping the validation tree returns only the table row. The table is otherwise actively curated, rows 18/22/23/24/32 carrying explicit 'retired, number never reused' markers, so row 26 is drift, not a retirement convention. The broad 'no binding to code' is a true structural observation but the only demonstrated drift is row 26.
C-architecture-04.survivingClaim: Confirmed narrowly on the concrete drift: registry row 26 asserts a live semantic rule for `simulation.sampling_scheme.type`, a field `deny_unknown_fields` now rejects at parse-time with a different ErrorKind, while curated retirements elsewhere prove the table is maintained, so the demonstrated defect is this one drifted row, the unbound prose registry being the mechanism rather than a second proven drift.
C-architecture-04.title: The semantic layer's rule registry is a prose table with no binding to code, and it has already drifted

C-architecture-05.argument: A stage-axis out-of-horizon rule for bound-override rows exists for exactly two families: thermal_bounds (thermal.rs:973, Layer 5a, `BusinessRuleViolation`) and ncs_bounds (referential.rs:944, Layer 3, `InvalidReference`). block_bounds.rs explicitly disclaims the stage axis in its doc (:96-99, 'skipped without a finding, that is a stage-axis defect this rule does not own'), and resolution/bounds.rs continues past any row whose stage_id is absent from `stage_index`. So for hydro/line/pumping/contract/hydro_unit_group bounds an out-of-horizon stage_id is silently dropped with no diagnostic, while the identical mistake on thermal or NCS is a hard load failure. Thermal's guard is family-motivated (its resolution table is padded to [n_stages, n_stages+K_max) for anticipated-delivery lookups, per its doc), but the five block-eligible families run the same study-stage-only resolver, so the silent-drop mechanism applies to them too and the coverage gap is real.
C-architecture-05.survivingClaim: Confirmed narrowly: the stage-axis out-of-horizon validator is missing for the five block-eligible non-thermal bound families (hydro/line/pumping/contract/hydro_unit_group), whose out-of-horizon rows are silently dropped by resolve_bounds, whereas thermal (5a) and NCS (Layer 3, different ErrorKind) reject hard, so the fix is to add the five missing checks; thermal's guard is legitimately family-specific (padded resolution region), making this a coverage/consistency gap rather than a claim that the two existing rules are misplaced.
C-architecture-05.title: An out-of-horizon `stage_id` on a bound-override row is a hard error for two families and a silent drop for the other five

C-architecture-06.argument: A file's presence is spelled in parallel lists that must agree by hand: `FILE_ENTRIES` (structural.rs:143), the `FileManifest` bool fields (:40), the fixed `[&mut bool; 43]` returned by `manifest_fields_mut` (:398), and again in `ParsedData`/schema.rs. `validate_structure` joins the first and third positionally (`FILE_ENTRIES.iter().zip(manifest_fields_mut(...))` at :376), and the code states the failure at :395-397 ('a divergence here silently misassigns presence flags'). The only guard (test_structural_manifest_fields_count, :612-623) asserts equal length by its own comment, so swapping two same-arity entries stays green while presence flags misassign. Adding a field is partly guarded (the fixed array arity plus the length test) but reordering is not. The `ParsedData`/schema.rs enumeration is a third restatement of the same set but is keyed by named field, not positionally joined, so it is a fan-out/DRY concern rather than a silent-misassignment one, and 'four lists joined by position' slightly over-states the join.
C-architecture-06.survivingClaim: Confirmed narrowly: the positional `FILE_ENTRIES` to `manifest_fields_mut` zip is guarded only by an equal-length assertion that cannot detect a same-arity reordering, so swapping two entries silently misassigns presence flags; the `ParsedData`/schema.rs list is a third parallel restatement of the file set but keyed by name (a DRY/fan-out concern), not part of the positional join.
C-architecture-06.title: The input-file registry is four hand-maintained parallel lists joined by position, guarded only by a length assertion

C-over-engineering-00.argument: At the baseline all three enums derive serde::Serialize plus schemars::JsonSchema under #[serde(rename_all="snake_case")] (estimation.rs:15-18, scenario_source.rs:70-73, training.rs:106-109), so each exports a string-only JSON enum schema. serde's DERIVED Deserialize for a unit-variant enum accepts both the bare string ("pacf") and serde's externally-tagged single-key-map form ({"pacf":null}); each hand-written impl deserializes via String::deserialize and matches only the bare string (estimation.rs:41-52, scenario_source.rs:84-99, training.rs:117-127). The impls are therefore strictly STRICTER than a derive and consistent with the published schema, whereas the finding's fix (replace with #[derive(Deserialize)]) would broaden acceptance to inputs the exported schema forbids. So the premise that they 'reimplement what the derive produces' is factually wrong. Each accepted-set list is additionally pinned by a rejection test in config/mod.rs (unknown_scheme/unknown_stopping_mode/order_selection_unknown_variant), so the intra-impl repetition is guarded, not floating.
C-over-engineering-00.title: Three hand-written `Deserialize` impls in `config/` reimplement what `#[derive(Deserialize)]` already produces, each duplicating its accepted-value list

C-over-engineering-01.argument: git grep default_severity across crates/ at the baseline returns only its declaration (validation/mod.rs:95) and the four asserts of test_error_kind_default_severity (validation/mod.rs:419-429); no production site calls it. Severity is chosen directly at each diagnostic by add_error (validation/mod.rs:157) or add_warning (validation/mod.rs:174). It is a pub method but no workspace crate consumes it and it is not a registered reserved seam. It has already drifted: the table maps BusinessRuleViolation to Severity::Error (everything except UnusedEntity/ModelQuality/SemanticAmbiguity), yet the only BusinessRuleViolation diagnostic in the tree is emitted via add_warning at season.rs:175-177. Because nothing reads the method, that disagreement cannot fail any test. Deleting the method and its tautological unit test leaves add_error/add_warning as the single severity owner; this is a cobre-io-local (L2) cleanup with no engine vocabulary, so layering is unaffected.
C-over-engineering-01.survivingClaim: default_severity (validation/mod.rs:95) has no caller outside its own unit test AND its BusinessRuleViolation->Error classification contradicts the sole BusinessRuleViolation emission (add_warning at season.rs:175-177); the defensible residue is an uncalled, already-divergent parallel severity table, conceding the title's 'purports to describe the call sites' framing since the method's doc only claims a per-kind default, never a mirror of the emission sites.
C-over-engineering-01.title: `ErrorKind::default_severity` is a public severity classification with zero callers, and it already disagrees with the call sites it purports to describe

C-over-engineering-02.argument: git grep 'data.penalties' returns nothing at the baseline; every .penalties read is hydro.penalties / h.penalties / a local penalties (scenarios.rs, hydros.rs, pipeline.rs:258 builder). ParsedData.penalties is constructed at schema.rs:667 and never read, so its #[allow(dead_code)] (schema.rs:74) silences a genuinely dead field; its rationale claims retention 'avoids re-reading penalties.json' for the Layer-5 penalty-ordering check, but that check reads per-entity hydro.penalties (scenarios.rs:179) while parsers take the local sentinel (schema.rs:273), so the stated saving does not occur, and the field is not a registered reserved seam. Conversely scalar_parameters IS live: validate_scalar_parameters(&data.scalar_parameters, ...) at pipeline.rs:96 and scalar_parameters: data.scalar_parameters at pipeline.rs:244, so the #[allow(dead_code)] at schema.rs:113 suppresses a lint that never fires. Neither attribute matches the #[allow] census class 'dead_code allow whose comment names a real future consumer'.
C-over-engineering-02.survivingClaim: ParsedData.penalties (schema.rs:75) has zero data.penalties reads workspace-wide and its rationale's saving is false (Layer-5 reads hydro.penalties at scenarios.rs:179, not the bundle); the scalar_parameters #[allow(dead_code)] (schema.rs:113) is merely REDUNDANT because the field is read at pipeline.rs:96 and moved at :244, so — narrowing the title — only its allow is stale while its rationale naming the resolution consumer is accurate.
C-over-engineering-02.title: Two `#[allow(dead_code)]` attributes on `ParsedData` carry rationales naming consumers that do not exist: `penalties` is genuinely never read, `scalar_parameters` is read and the allow is stale

C-over-engineering-03.argument: Counts verified at baseline: 43 pub bool fields on FileManifest, 43 FileEntry rows in FILE_ENTRIES (the 44th 'FileEntry {' hit is the struct declaration), and 43 &mut m.<field> entries in manifest_fields_mut returning [&mut bool; 43]. validate_structure joins FILE_ENTRIES and manifest_fields_mut by position (structural.rs:376). The helper's own doc (structural.rs:396-397) states 'a divergence here silently misassigns presence flags', and the only guard, test_structural_manifest_fields_count (structural.rs:612-623), compares lengths only and says so in its comment ('the invariant is length, not any specific count'). With 8 required files and the rest optional, transposing two optional rows keeps both the length test and the eight-missing-required-files test green while every downstream manifest.<field> read (38 occurrences in schema.rs) observes the wrong file's flag. The design is behaviour-correct for the current ordering but unguarded against reordering. Any fix stays inside cobre-io (L2) with no engine vocabulary, so layering is unaffected.
C-over-engineering-03.survivingClaim: The defect is the ORDER-unguarded positional zip between FILE_ENTRIES and manifest_fields_mut (structural.rs:376): the sole guard asserts equal length only (structural.rs:612-623, comment: length not order), so swapping any two same-required-ness optional rows silently misassigns presence flags exactly as the helper's doc warns (structural.rs:396-397) while all tests stay green; conceding the title's 'three redundant lists' framing, the named-bool struct itself earns its place via the type-checked manifest.<field> reads in schema.rs, so the residue is the unguarded order coupling, not the existence of named fields.
C-over-engineering-03.title: `FileManifest` presence tracking is three hand-maintained 43-element lists zipped positionally, with a hand-rolled `[&mut bool; 43]` reflection helper and only a length guard

C-perf-00.argument: At the baseline merged_windows_for_hydro (inflow_seeding.rs:181) scans data.inflow_history in full and filters to one hydro (185), and does the same over recent_observations, allocating three fresh Vecs. check_slot_coverage builds a per-hydro map via data.hydros.iter().map(|h| (h.id.0, merged_windows_for_hydro(data,h.id))) at 244, so the two full-table scans repeat once per hydro (O(hydros x rows)); check_inprogress_partial_coverage repeats the identical construction inside for hydro in &data.hydros at 339. Both rules live in the same entry point validate_inflow_seeding (28). The nested per-hydro scan is real for each rule. The cross-rule duplicate construction, however, only materializes when BOTH preconditions hold: check_slot_coverage returns early when data.inflow_ar_coefficients.is_empty() and when l_state==0, while check_inprogress only needs season_map/first_stage/season resolution, so on an estimation-only deck the merged windows are built just once.
C-perf-00.survivingClaim: The nested O(hydros x [inflow_history + recent_observations] rows) filter in merged_windows_for_hydro (181/185) is paid once per hydro inside each of check_slot_coverage (244) and check_inprogress_partial_coverage (339); the ADDITIONAL cross-rule duplicate construction of the same per-hydro merged map only occurs when both rules' preconditions hold at once (inflow_ar_coefficients non-empty and l_state > 0), not on every deck.
C-perf-00.title: `merged_windows_for_hydro` filters the whole inflow-history table per hydro, and two independent seeding rules each build the same per-hydro map from scratch

C-perf-01.argument: At the baseline check_prefix_coherence (scenarios.rs ~832) loops for tr in &graph.transitions, and inside for each class walks for s in 0..=sn doing class.entities.iter().find_map with two class.cells.get lookups per entity (854-855). The compared cells depend only on (class, cn, cm, s); nothing inside the three nested loops reads the edge except the warning text (tr.source_id/target_id). Because the s-loop restarts at 0 for every transition, two transitions that share the same source column cn, target column cm, and source stage depth sn re-do byte-identical cell comparisons. The re-walk is bounded by the find_map/break: on the first disagreeing stage the walk stops, so the full 0..=sn prefix is re-scanned only in the no-disagreement (valid) case. Eliminating the redundancy by comparing each distinct column pair once changes the per-edge warning attribution (one representative edge instead of one warning per edge) unless the per-edge loop is kept with a decided-pair short-circuit.
C-perf-01.survivingClaim: check_prefix_coherence (846-857) re-walks stages 0..=sn per transition and re-does identical cell comparisons for any two transitions sharing (source column cn, target column cm, source stage depth sn); the redundancy is real specifically in the no-disagreement case (find_map+break bounds the walk once a stage disagrees), and de-duplicating to once-per-pair alters per-edge warning attribution unless the per-edge loop is retained with a decided-pair short-circuit.
C-perf-01.title: Prefix-coherence re-walks the entire root prefix for every graph edge, so a repeated column pair is compared once per edge instead of once per pair

C-perf-02.argument: extract_class (scenarios.rs:647) builds cells (647), union_by_stage (649), entity_scen (650) and, for the inflow class only, inflow_sample_rows (651), inserting into each per row in one loop (665/684/685-688/694). The sole reader of cells VALUES is check_prefix_coherence at 855, and that call is guarded at 620 by !data.stages.policy_graph.nodes.is_empty(); check_raw_c_agreement (798) reads raw_c not cells. So on a chain-dialect deck (nodes empty) the f64 values in cells are built and dropped unread, though the cells MAP keys are still needed for the in-build duplicate-key detection (insert().is_some(), ~671). The broader 'four full-table-sized structures per external class' over-reaches: inflow_sample_rows is materialized for the inflow class only (name=="inflow" guard at 693-694), so load/ncs classes build three; and union_by_stage is a per-stage union of distinct scenario_ids, bounded above by the row count but typically smaller than a full table copy. entity_scen and cells are the genuinely full-table-sized indices of the same (stage, scenario, entity) triples.
C-perf-02.survivingClaim: On a chain-dialect deck (data.stages.policy_graph.nodes empty, guard at 620) extract_class's cells map retains f64 values no rule reads (its only value reader check_prefix_coherence at 855 is skipped) while the map keys are still used for in-build duplicate detection; the wider 'four full-table structures per class' is narrowed because inflow_sample_rows is inflow-class-only (693-694) and union_by_stage is bounded by distinct scenario_ids per stage rather than the full row count.
C-perf-02.title: `extract_class` materializes four full-table-sized structures per external class, one of which carries values no rule reads on the chain dialect

C-perf-03.argument: Three sites declare the byte-identical index Vec<(NaiveDate,NaiveDate,usize)> via the same filter_map(|s| s.season_id.map(|sid| (s.start_date,s.end_date,sid))) — season.rs:141, season.rs:264, scenarios.rs:1012 — and each then runs stage_index.partition_point(|(start,_,_)| *start <= row.start_date) in a for row in &data.inflow_history loop (150/273/1026). All three sit under the estimation-active predicate has_history && !(has_stats && has_ar) (season.rs:127-135, season.rs:246-250 in equivalent form, scenarios.rs:966-973). The shared work is genuinely triplicated. But the per-row work downstream of partition_point is NOT identical: check_observation_season_alignment adds an .or_else(season_map.season_for_date) fallback and counts (hydro,season,year); check_season_observation_coverage has no fallback and counts per season; check_estimation_prerequisites resolves to a stage-occurrence bucket and applies cast() coverage-gating, not a season count. Nor do all three always fire together: check_season_observation_coverage additionally returns when the training inflow scheme is External, and check_estimation_prerequisites builds its index only inside the season_map.is_some() block (1011). 'Three modules' is really three functions across two files.
C-perf-03.survivingClaim: The identical stage_index build (season.rs:141, season.rs:264, scenarios.rs:1012) and the identical partition_point predecessor lookup over data.inflow_history are triplicated under the shared estimation-active predicate; the narrowed residue is that shared index+lookup only, NOT a fully-shared season resolution (site 1 adds an .or_else season_for_date fallback, site 3 resolves to stage-occurrence + cast() coverage gating rather than a season), and the three do not always co-fire (site 2 requires non-External inflow scheme, site 3's index needs season_map present).
C-perf-03.title: Three modules build the same sorted stage-window index and re-run the same per-row season resolution over the inflow-history table under one shared precondition

C-perf-04.argument: slot_occupying_classes (stages.rs:357) filters data.external_scenarios, data.external_load_scenarios and data.external_ncs_scenarios in full for a single stage_id (371/382/393) and distinct_count (403) collects each survivor set into a fresh HashSet<i32>. check_realization_rules calls it at 308 inside for node in nodes (304), so the up-to-three-table scan and set allocations repeat once per declared node — and since the result depends only on stage_id, every node sharing a stage recomputes the identical value: that per-node redundancy is the strongest residue because nodes >= distinct stages in a scenario tree/lattice. check_num_openings_declaration (667) and check_sampling_method_meaningfulness (797) call it once per DISTINCT staged stage (staged is built by collecting node stage_ids into a HashSet then sorting), so those two are per-stage, not per-node. The identical per-stage distinct-scenario-id count is already produced in one pass as ClassExternal.raw_c (scenarios.rs:536, filled ~716), so the value has an owner, but reusing it crosses the scenarios.rs<->stages.rs module and precondition boundary rather than being an in-function share.
C-perf-04.survivingClaim: slot_occupying_classes (357) full-scans up to three external tables plus a fresh HashSet per call, and check_realization_rules invokes it once per node (308 inside for node in nodes) so nodes sharing a stage recompute an identical stage-keyed result — that per-node redundancy is the solid defect; call sites 667/797 recompute once per DISTINCT staged stage (staged is already deduped), not per node, and the sibling ClassExternal.raw_c (536/716) holds the same count in one pass but reusing it is a cross-module (scenarios.rs->stages.rs) share, not a free local one.
C-perf-04.title: `slot_occupying_classes` re-scans all three external scenario tables once per graph node and once per staged stage, recomputing a per-stage column count the sibling module already builds in one pass

C-test-bloat-00.argument: At baseline error.rs:152-247, test_load_error_io_display and test_load_error_io_helper both construct via the same LoadError::io helper and assert display contains(path) + contains(source-message), differing only in string literals plus io_helper's added matches!(err, IoError { .. }); so they are near-duplicates, not the six-way tautology the title implies. The per-variant contains walks also guard that each #[error("...{field}...")] attribute (error.rs:30-101) still names its context fields, a real if weak regression guard, and test_load_error_is_std_error (230) additionally checks the &dyn Error coercion and source().is_none(). The defensible residue is the IoError near-duplication plus test_load_error_schema_display (181) overlapping the module's own rustdoc doctest (error.rs:17-27, which already asserts contains("bus_id")).
C-test-bloat-00.survivingClaim: The two IoError tests (test_load_error_io_display @152 and test_load_error_io_helper @240) are near-duplicates -- both build via LoadError::io and assert the same path+source contains facts, differing only in literals plus one matches! -- so one is redundant; and test_load_error_schema_display @181 re-covers the contains("bus_id") fact the module doctest at error.rs:27 already asserts.
C-test-bloat-00.title: `error.rs`'s six inline tests assert only that thiserror interpolates the format strings declared a hundred lines above them, and two of the six are the same test twice

C-test-bloat-01.argument: Verified at baseline: generate_schemas (schema.rs:88) builds 18 entries and schemas/ holds 18 committed files, yet the doctest (line 84) and test_generate_schemas_returns_expected_count (166) assert only >= 17, so deleting one export passes a test named for an expected count. The CI schemas job (ci.yml:338-339 -> check_schemas.sh diff -ruN) is a byte-exact oracle, but it only catches a deletion that leaves schemas/ un-regenerated; a regenerate-blind deletion of one of the 5 schemas NOT pinned by name in test_all_expected_schema_filenames_present (which lists 13) is caught by nothing and tolerated by the >= 17 floor. tests 2/3/4 (172/182/193) each re-run full generation to assert generic properties (!is_null subset is_object subset has-structural-key) any real schema satisfies. I narrow away the title's implication that CI makes these pointless -- they run at unit speed and survive regeneration -- but the loose floor and 3-way structural redundancy are real.

D-architecture-00.argument: Verified at baseline: atomic.rs opens 'Single owner of the write-side crash-safety contract: write to {path}.tmp, flush explicitly, then rename', yet checkpoint.rs imports nothing from it and uses four bare std::fs::write calls (:221 :227 :237 :244), the last being manifest.bin at :244 whose own comment calls it 'the commit signal'; dictionary.rs writes entities.csv via csv::Writer::from_path (:148) and variables.csv (:256) directly onto the final name. Both csv writers and std::fs::write truncate the final path (O_TRUNC) before writing, so an interrupted write destroys the prior good file in place - exactly the loss tmp-then-rename prevents - falsifying the 'single owner' doc. The per-payload cuts/basis/states .bin writes are additionally covered at the artifact level by the manifest-last commit signal (a crash before manifest leaves an artifact the reader rejects), so the load-bearing crash-safety residue is the in-place overwrites of manifest.bin and the two CSVs, not the payload .bin files.
D-architecture-00.survivingClaim: The crash-safety hole is specifically the in-place (O_TRUNC) overwrites of manifest.bin at checkpoint.rs:244 and of entities.csv/variables.csv in dictionary.rs, which can leave a truncated file replacing the previous good one; the cuts/basis/states .bin payload writes are covered by the manifest-last commit-signal design and are not an independent crash-safety hole.
D-architecture-00.title: atomic.rs declares itself sole owner of the write-side crash-safety contract, but the policy checkpoint and two dictionary CSVs bypass it entirely

D-architecture-01.argument: Verified at baseline: output/mod.rs:6-8 states 'The top-level entry point is write_results, which mirrors crate::load_case: it accepts aggregate result types and writes all output artifacts to the specified directory.' But write_results at results_writer.rs:166 only calls write_training_results and write_simulation_results (reaching write_dictionaries, TrainingParquetWriter, and the two metadata writers). The real orchestration is in crates/cobre-cli/src/commands/run/outputs.rs, which bypasses write_results entirely: it calls write_training_results and write_simulation_results directly plus ~13 further writers (write_fpha_hyperplanes :95, write_evaporation_models :107, write_fpha_deviation_points :119, write_generic_constraint_echo :134, write_fixed_delivery :138, write_solver_stats :142, write_row_selection_records :147, write_paths :212, write_scenario_summary :221), with hand-mirror comments ('mirror on the Python side'). So the doc's 'writes all output artifacts / mirrors load_case' claim is objectively false and the aggregate contract is not honoured.
D-architecture-01.survivingClaim: The confirmed defect is narrowly the false module-doc contract at output/mod.rs:6-8 (write_results does not 'write all output artifacts' and does not mirror load_case) and the resulting undocumented CLI/Python hand-mirror; it does not establish that write_results must be expanded to orchestrate every artifact - that consolidation is the 0a design choice, not part of the present defect.
D-architecture-01.title: write_results is documented as the top-level output entry point mirroring load_case, but reaches 5 of the crate's 27 output writers, so cobre-io publishes an aggregate contract it does not honour

D-architecture-02.argument: Verified at baseline: schemas.rs:1 module doc says 'Arrow schema definitions for all Parquet output files', but a schema-fn census shows 34 total (25 in schemas.rs, 5 in stochastic.rs, 3 in hydro_models.rs, 1 in dictionary.rs). Two hand-maintained enumerations then claim family-wide reach and both fall short: variables_csv_schemas() lists 22 of 34 while write_variables_csv's doc says 'one row per column across every output schema', and the gate test one_spelling_per_axis_across_every_output_schema at schemas.rs:1346 iterates a 21-entry literal list while its own comment asserts 'a later file cannot reintroduce a variant without failing this one test'. Because noise_openings_schema and the inflow_* family are among the 13 omitted, a forbidden axis spelling (e.g. 'stage' or 'opening') introduced in one of those sibling-declared schemas would never be checked - the guard's stated coverage exceeds its actual coverage (doc-integrity 3 mode 6, false-confidence guard).
D-architecture-02.survivingClaim: The load-bearing, concretely-defective residue is the over-broad self-description of the two enumerations versus their partial hand-maintained lists - chiefly the axis-spelling gate's 'a later file cannot reintroduce a variant without failing this one test' asserted over a 21-of-34 subset; the wider 'no single owner' framing is the shape of the fix, not itself the proven defect.
D-architecture-02.title: The output Arrow-schema family has no single owner: 34 schemas across 4 modules, and both the shipped data dictionary and the axis-spelling gate enumerate a hand-maintained subset

D-architecture-03.argument: Verified at baseline: convergence_schema (:365) declares cuts_added/cuts_removed/cuts_active/time_forward_ms/time_backward_ms/forward_passes/lower_bound/upper_bound/gap_percent; iteration_timing_schema (:398) declares cut_selection_ms/cut_sync_ms/cut_batch_build_ms/bwd_*/fwd_*/lazy_scoring_ms; row_selection_schema (:516) declares five cuts_* columns; IterationRecord carries the mirror fields. These are SDDP training-loop names living in the L2 cobre-io crate. The gate scripts/ci/check-infra-genericity.sh:79 uses word-boundary patterns and its OWN comment names 'cuts_active' as an identifier it must not flag, so snake_case compounds evade it and the gate exits 0 over this surface. Part-I I.3-6 in partI-handoff.json covers only the FlatBuffers value-function format (PolicyCutRecord/StageCutsPayload/StageCuts), not this Parquet/struct surface. I concede this is NOT a violation of the ratified genericity contract, which enumerates sddp/SDDP/Benders plus standalone cut - none of which these column names contain - so no immediate rename is warranted; the confirmed residue is the unregistered, oracle-invisible coupling.
D-architecture-03.survivingClaim: The confirmed defect is the register/oracle-coverage gap only: the Parquet convergence/timing/row_selection schemas and IterationRecord carry training-loop column names that Part-I I.3-6 does not name and the word-boundary genericity gate deliberately cannot see; it is expressly NOT an enforced-contract violation (the ratified sddp/SDDP/Benders/standalone-cut tokens are absent) and requires no rename now - only widening the I.3-6 disposition.
D-architecture-03.title: The training-loop vocabulary is baked into the L2 output schema surface as on-disk column names, a coupling the genericity oracle structurally cannot see and no Part-I item names

D-architecture-04.argument: Verified at baseline: the entity-family list is enumerated twice in simulation_writer.rs with two predicate sets. new() (:587-651) gates directory creation on system-shaped predicates (system.n_hydros()>0, system.n_lines()>0, a declares_travel_time arc scan, a declares_post_study scan); write_scenario (:728+) gates the actual write on payload-shaped predicates (result.stages.iter().any(|s| !s.hydros.is_empty()) and siblings). write_partition at :687 itself calls create_dir_all on the full partition path, so new()'s create_dir_all calls are redundant in the populated case and observable only when a family is system-declared but never populated - which is exactly the case write_scenario's doc at :696-697 promises cannot leave a directory ('no directory is created'), contradicting new()'s doc at :558-560 that it 'Creates ... one entity subdirectory per entity type with a non-zero count'. Two doc comments thus state incompatible contracts about the same output-tree property and nothing binds the two predicate sets.
D-architecture-04.survivingClaim: The confirmed defect is the unreconciled duplication plus the contradictory documented contract for the empty-family case (new() creates a directory for a system-declared-but-payload-empty family, which write_scenario's doc says cannot exist), with new()'s create_dir_all otherwise redundant against write_partition's own create_dir_all; the two predicate sets are each locally sensible and this is not a runtime data-corruption bug.
D-architecture-04.title: SimulationParquetWriter answers "which entity families does this run emit" twice, with different inputs and contradicting doc comments, inside one file

D-architecture-05.argument: Verified at baseline: parquet_helpers.rs:1 is the read side's single owner ('Shared Parquet column extraction helpers centralising the typed-downcast logic used by every Parquet parser in cobre-io'). The write side has no counterpart module: its one shared helper ensure_parent_dir is declared pub(crate) inside output/stochastic.rs:451 (a domain writer for inflow/load statistics) and imported across the domain boundary by fixed_delivery.rs:24, generic_constraints_echo.rs:20 and hydro_models.rs:39. Meanwhile scaling_report.rs:24 and provenance.rs:26 re-open-code the exact three-line body ('if let Some(parent) = path.parent() { std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|e| OutputError::io(parent, e))?; }') instead of importing it. Downstream the four-line prologue (ensure_parent_dir, ParquetWriterConfig::default, build_x_batch, write_parquet_atomic) recurs across four modules. This is a placement/duplication asymmetry the read side does not have.
D-architecture-05.survivingClaim: The concrete defensible defect is the cross-domain mis-homing of ensure_parent_dir inside stochastic.rs (imported by three unrelated writers) together with its two verbatim open-coded copies in scaling_report.rs:24 and provenance.rs:26; the 'ten identical prologues' is the broader repetition a fix would fold, not itself the load-bearing residue.
D-architecture-05.title: The write path has no helper module answering to parquet_helpers.rs: its one shared helper is homed inside a domain writer, two modules re-open-code it, and the identical write prologue repeats ten times

D-over-engineering-00.argument: At the baseline write_dictionaries (dictionary.rs:68) declares `_config: &Config` (line 71), the underscore marking it declared-and-never-read; its body calls write_codes_json / write_entities_csv / write_variables_csv / write_bounds_parquet and hands config to none. D-over-engineering-01.argument: Both default_upper_bound_kind (manifest.rs:220) and default_bounds (manifest.rs:227) exist only to back a same-module serde default-path attribute (manifest.rs:214 and manifest.rs:412); serde resolves those path strings against the surrounding module, so a private fn suffices and pub adds nothing. default_bounds is additionally re-exported to the crate root at output/mod.rs:47 with zero external consumers, but default_upper_bound_kind is NOT in that re-export list, so it is pub inside a private module and unreachable externally. Neither is dead code (each has an attribute or internal caller: default_bounds calls default_upper_bound_kind at manifest.rs:232), so the residue is over-visibility, not deadness. Narrowing visibility is a pure local cleanup with no layering movement.
D-over-engineering-01.survivingClaim: The narrower defect is needless pub visibility: both functions back only a same-module serde default-path attribute where a private fn suffices; and contra the title only default_bounds is actually crate-root public API (re-exported at output/mod.rs:47, zero external callers), while default_upper_bound_kind is pub but never re-exported, so it is merely pub inside a private module.
D-over-engineering-01.title: `default_bounds` and `default_upper_bound_kind` are serde-attribute helpers published as crate-root public API with no consumer anywhere

D-over-engineering-02.argument: A workspace grep for a read of either field returns nothing (exit 1); the only assignments are the struct-literal producer at training_output.rs:234,237. The WorkerTimingRecord conversion loop for convergence_records (training_output.rs:517-530) copies eleven other time_* fields into slots but conspicuously omits slots 8 and 11. The bwd_setup_ms / fwd_setup_ms Parquet columns (training_writer.rs:258,261) read rec.timings[8] / [11], which only the per-worker path fills from WorkerPhaseTimings (training_output.rs:505-508). IterationRecord derives only Debug, Clone (mod.rs:76), so there is no serde escape hatch. The two doc arrows at mod.rs:141,149 assert a mapping the per-iteration record never supplies. Deleting the two fields (or wiring slots 8/11 from them) is a local cleanup with no layering effect.
D-over-engineering-02.survivingClaim: The defect is exactly the two fields IterationRecord.time_bwd_setup_ms (mod.rs:141) and time_fwd_setup_ms (mod.rs:149): they are the only two time_* fields the convergence-path conversion loop skips (slots 8 and 11, training_output.rs:517-530), so they are populated at training_output.rs:234,237 and read nowhere; the columns they doc-arrow to are real but fed solely from the per-worker WorkerPhaseTimings path, not from IterationRecord.
D-over-engineering-02.title: `IterationRecord.time_bwd_setup_ms` and `time_fwd_setup_ms` are write-only public fields whose doc arrows promise a Parquet column the writer feeds from a different source

D-over-engineering-03.argument: The struct-literal grep returns only the declaration (parquet_config.rs:24) and the Default impl (line 38); no site anywhere builds a non-default ParquetWriterConfig, and the sole field write is the clone-independence test at parquet_config.rs:90. Every production, CLI and Python site uses ::default() (run/outputs.rs:146, run/simulation.rs:77, run.rs:512, run.rs:679). The type is not schema-exported (no JsonSchema derive, grep exit 1) and the only input key that could feed it, exports.compression, is a rejected deny_unknown_fields legacy key (config/exports.rs:9-14). It is therefore not a reserved seam: the register holds only transit_bucket_topology, LipschitzConfig and the cobre-comm shared-memory hierarchy, and the CLAUDE.md unwired-config rule covers config that is loaded, validated and schema-exported, none of which is true here. The threading is also asymmetric: write_parquet_atomic (atomic.rs:112), TrainingParquetWriter::new (training_writer.rs:84), SimulationParquetWriter::new (simulation_writer.rs:570) and write_bounds_parquet (dictionary.rs:822) take the parameter while ~13 writers rebuild a local default (e.g. stochastic.rs:130).
D-over-engineering-03.survivingClaim: Conceding the struct is not dead (its three fields are read by every parquet writer) and that pinning the encoding values is itself justified by the binary-formats spec (parquet_config.rs:5) and output-byte comparability, the narrower defect is the caller-varied-config machinery: no path constructs a non-default value, exports.compression is a rejected input, and the &ParquetWriterConfig parameter is threaded through only four functions while ~13 production writers rebuild the default locally, so the variability has no present consumer and cannot be honored uniformly.
D-over-engineering-03.title: `ParquetWriterConfig` is a configurability surface no shipped caller can vary: never constructed except via `Default`, and half the writers rebuild the default locally instead of accepting the parameter

D-over-engineering-04.argument: read_f32_vector_as_f64 resolves exactly once at the baseline, at its own declaration (codec.rs:575) - no production caller, test, or re-export. policy.fbs declares zero float32 fields, so the case it reserves against has never arrived. It carries the sub-station's only #[allow(dead_code)] (codec.rs:574). Its rationale comment cites completeness/symmetry and adding an f32 field later but names no owner and no landing reader, so it fails the reserved-seam #[allow] census class; and no test exercises it, so it fails the symmetry-or-test-retention class. The neighbours read_f64_vector, read_u32_vector and read_u8_vector sit immediately beside it and demonstrate the identical bounds-checked shape, so the pattern is not at risk of being lost. Deleting it is a local cleanup that touches only codec.rs and does not affect layering.
D-over-engineering-04.survivingClaim: Conceding the byte-parsing body itself is correct and harmless (a faithful mirror of read_f64_vector), the narrower defect is purely its retention as dead code: at baseline the symbol resolves only at codec.rs:575, carries the scope's sole #[allow(dead_code)] (codec.rs:574), and its comment names neither owner nor landing reader, so it qualifies as neither sanctioned #[allow] census class.
D-over-engineering-04.title: `read_f32_vector_as_f64` is a dead codec reader kept by a completeness rationale, with no caller, no test and no f32 field in the schema it mirrors

D-over-engineering-05.argument: run_pipeline (pipeline.rs:47) is one .map discarding the report; run_pipeline_with_report (pipeline.rs:57) is one .map projecting LoadedCase to its System field; only run_pipeline_with_artifacts (pipeline.rs:73) does work. Each adapter has exactly one caller, and that caller is itself a one-line lib.rs adapter: load_case (lib.rs:235) calls run_pipeline, validate_case (lib.rs:266) calls run_pipeline_with_report. So load_case reaches the work through three consecutive projections. run_pipeline_with_artifacts has two direct callers (lib.rs:252,285). The four public entry points already own four distinct return shapes; the pipeline layer re-derives two of them a second time with no additional consumer and no direct test caller (grep shows callers only in lib.rs). Collapsing the two adapters touches only pipeline.rs and lib.rs and is neutral to layering.
D-over-engineering-05.survivingClaim: Conceding run_pipeline_with_artifacts is the legitimate working function and the four public lib.rs entry points each justify a distinct return shape, the narrower defect is the two pub(crate) intermediates run_pipeline (pipeline.rs:47) and run_pipeline_with_report (pipeline.rs:57): each is a one-line .map projection with exactly one caller that is itself a one-line lib.rs adapter (lib.rs:235 and lib.rs:266), so each re-derives a shape the public entry points already own and can be folded into its caller with no loss of any contract or caller.
D-over-engineering-05.title: Two of the three functions in `pipeline.rs` are pure one-caller adapters, so the crate's main load entry point crosses three forwarding hops before any work happens

D-perf-00.argument: At baseline the four serializers end with builder.finished_data().to_vec() (codec.rs:284/333/365/455), and write_policy_checkpoint (checkpoint.rs:220-244) binds each returned Vec to buf, borrows it as a slice for std::fs::write, and drops it on the next line, so the to_vec() is a genuine full-buffer memcpy the write path never needs since finished_data() already yields a sufficient &[u8]. Narrowing: the serializers are pub with doctests that call them standalone (serialize_stage_basis's doc constructs a record and asserts on the buffer), so the owned-Vec return is justified for external/doctest callers; only the internal checkpoint path can shed the copy, and it is paid at checkpoint-write cadence (one memcpy per .bin file per checkpoint), not on the training hot loop.
D-perf-00.survivingClaim: The internal checkpoint write path pays an avoidable full-buffer memcpy: each serializer's finished_data().to_vec() (codec.rs:284/333/365/455) is copied only for fs::write in checkpoint.rs:221/227/237/244 to borrow it as a slice and drop it, but the copy occurs at checkpoint cadence and the owned-Vec return stays justified for the pub API's doctest/external callers.
D-perf-00.title: Every policy artifact is copied out of the FlatBuffers builder into a fresh `Vec` that exists only to be handed to `fs::write`

D-perf-01.argument: Confirmed by reading the code: build_costs_batch (simulation_writer.rs:1076) opens let schema = Arc::new(costs_schema()), and costs_schema (schemas.rs:22-53) plus simulation_row_prefix (schemas.rs:10-16) construct every Field::new with a fresh heap column-name String on each call, so a fully populated scenario rebuilds the whole run-invariant field list once per scenario. Separately write_parquet_atomic (atomic.rs:109-114) rebuilds WriterProperties from the caller's already-resolved ParquetWriterConfig on every file. Both depend on nothing per-scenario. Narrowing: these are fixed-size, data-volume-independent overheads amortized against the per-scenario RecordBatch fill and Parquet encode/compress they accompany, so the residue is a bounded per-scenario/per-file allocation removable via a process-lifetime shared Arc<Schema> handle and a once-resolved properties value, not a cost that scales with row count.
D-perf-01.survivingClaim: Each build_*_batch reconstructs its run-invariant Arrow Field list (with fresh column-name Strings) once per scenario (simulation_writer.rs:1076; schemas.rs:10-53) and write_parquet_atomic rebuilds WriterProperties per file (atomic.rs:109-114): a bounded, data-volume-independent per-scenario/per-file allocation, not a row-count-scaling cost.
D-perf-01.title: Every per-scenario partition write rebuilds a run-invariant Arrow schema and a run-invariant Parquet `WriterProperties`

D-perf-02.argument: Verified against the metadata sink: SimulationMetadata (manifest.rs:434-462) has no partition field, and write_simulation_results (results_writer.rs:133-155) builds the metadata from simulation_output reading only total_time_ms, n_scenarios, completed, failed, cost, and solve_stats, never partitions_written. Yet write_partition (simulation_writer.rs:690) pushes a format! path per partition, finalize (:941) moves the list into SimulationOutput, merge (mod.rs:431-435) clones and sorts it, and the distributed CLI (simulation.rs:305-357) joins it to bytes and allgathervs it so every rank materializes every rank's paths, and the merged value reaches no output file.
